metadata.name: HP ZBook x2 G4 PCH root port PME storm on GPE 0x69

data.summary: No more interrupt storm from the chipset after the SD card is pulled or a dock is attached; it used to keep a CPU core busy until reboot.

reproduced20261011.reason: BIOS P72 01.53, kernel 7.2.2. Removing the SD card while the RTS522A reader (02:00.0) sleeps in D3hot makes it send a PME; root port #3 (00:1c.2) has PMEX (config 0xD8 bit 31) set and latches PMSX (0xDC bit 31), which raises GPE 0x69. The firmware's _L69 is empty and platform _OSC aborts (AE_AML_BUFFER_LIMIT), so nothing clears PMSX: about 7,700 GPEs per second until reboot. Clearing PMSX stopped it (7,510/s to 0). With PMEX cleared, pulling and reinserting the card raised no GPE and Linux still saw the card go and come back through its PME polling. BIOS 01.53 is the newest HP release for board 824C.

reproduced20261011b.reason: BIOS P72 01.53, kernel 7.2.2. With a USB-C dock attached at boot, Thunderbolt root port #5 (00:1c.4, JHL6540 behind it) latched PMSX with PMEX set and GPE 0x69 ran at about 7,750 per second, irq/9-acpi using 86% of a core. Clearing PMEX and PMSX on 00:1c.4 stopped it (7,753/s to 0). All five PCH root ports (9d10 NVIDIA, 9d12 card reader, 9d13 Wi-Fi, 9d14 Thunderbolt, 9d18 NVMe) route PME to the same GPE 0x69, whose _L69 handler is empty, so routing a PME there never helps on any of them; Linux handles root port PME natively.
